initiatives.name: Board Governance and Oversight Evolution
initiatives.summary: Following the Nomination Committee's review, the Board approved uplifts to Directors' fees across multiple roles, including a new Nomination Committee Chair fee introduced at £3,000 per annum, effective from 1 May 2025.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £85,000 (Chair's fee); £37,500 (NED base fee); £12,000 (Audit Chair); £3,000 (Nomination Chair); £5,000 (Marketing Chair)

evidence.title: Director resignation and Board gender composition change
evidence.summary: Andrew Ross resigned from the Board effective 31 December 2025, leaving the Board composed of one male and five female directors, meeting Listing Rules diversity targets for gender and ethnic representation.
evidence.quote: Following the resignation of Andrew Ross on 31 December 2025, the Board at the year end comprised one male and five females.

evidence.title: External Board evaluation by Stogdale St James
evidence.summary: Following a tender process, the Board appointed Stogdale St James in July 2025 to conduct an externally facilitated evaluation of Board and Committee effectiveness, postponed from the prior year due to the Alliance Trust/Witan combination. Findings were presented to the Board in October 2025.
evidence.quote: In July 2025, following a thorough tender process led by Sarah Bates and Rachel Beagles, the Board approved, on the recommendation of the Nomination Committee, the appointment of Stogdale St James to conduct the externally facilitated evaluation of the Board and its Committees.

evidence.title: Director fee increases and new Nomination Committee Chair fee
evidence.summary: Following the Nomination Committee's review, the Board approved uplifts to Directors' fees across multiple roles, including a new Nomination Committee Chair fee introduced at £3,000 per annum, effective from 1 May 2025.
evidence.quote: Chair's fee increased from £80,000 to £85,000 per annum... Nomination Committee Chair fee introduced at £3,000 per annum... All changes were effective from 1 May 2025.

evidence.title: Marketing Oversight Group upgraded to full Board Committee
evidence.summary: Effective 1 January 2026, the Board approved evolving the Marketing Oversight Group from a working group into a formal Marketing Committee of the Board, reflecting the increasing importance of marketing in serving shareholders and attracting new investors. The Committee is chaired by Milyae Park.
evidence.quote: With effect from 1 January 2026, the Board approved the evolution of the Marketing Oversight Group from a working group of the Board to an established Committee of the Board – the Marketing Committee – in recognition of the important role that marketing plays in serving the needs of shareholders and attracting new investors.

initiatives.name: Alliance Trust and Witan Combination
initiatives.summary: Alliance Trust combined with Witan in October 2024, creating an enlarged company that is now part of the FTSE 100, enhancing liquidity and providing a platform for shareholder base growth. The combination's costs were partially offset by a management fee waiver from the Investment Manager.

evidence.title: Combination with Witan forms FTSE 100 company
evidence.summary: Alliance Trust combined with Witan in October 2024, creating an enlarged company that is now part of the FTSE 100, enhancing liquidity and providing a platform for shareholder base growth. The combination's costs were partially offset by a management fee waiver from the Investment Manager.
evidence.quote: The enlarged size of the Company, now a FTSE 100 company after the combination with Witan in October 2024, enhances liquidity and provides a strong platform from which to grow the shareholder base.

evidence.title: Management fee waiver offsets Witan combination costs
evidence.summary: The Investment Manager (WTW) negotiated a fee waiver to contribute toward the costs of the Company's combination with Witan, reducing the Ongoing Charges Ratio. This waiver was spread over 12 months from the date of combination, directly reducing costs in both 2024 and 2025.
evidence.quote: The Company's ongoing charges ratio ('OCR') decreased to 0.47% (2024: 0.56%) reflecting the management fee waiver negotiated with the Investment Manager in respect of its contribution to the costs of the Company's combination with Witan (excluding the management fee waiver the OCR was 0.59%).

initiatives.name: Share Buyback Programme 2025
initiatives.summary: The Company bought back 17.8 million shares (4.7% of issued share capital) during 2025 at a total cost of £223.6 million, up significantly from £57.0 million in 2024, as part of its strategy to manage the share price discount to NAV. Shares were placed in Treasury for potential future reissue at a premium to NAV.

evidence.title: £223.6m share buyback programme in 2025
evidence.summary: The Company bought back 17.8 million shares (4.7% of issued share capital) during 2025 at a total cost of £223.6 million, up significantly from £57.0 million in 2024, as part of its strategy to manage the share price discount to NAV. Shares were placed in Treasury for potential future reissue at a premium to NAV.
evidence.quote: The Company bought back 4.7%* (2024: 1.2%) of its issued share capital during the year, purchasing 17,837,838 shares which were placed in Treasury. The total cost of the share buybacks was £223.6m (2024: £57.0m).

initiatives.name: Stock Picker Portfolio Optimization
initiatives.summary: WTW removed ARGA and SGA as Stock Pickers due to operational issues and personnel changes respectively, replacing them with Brown Advisory and Artisan Partners to improve portfolio quality and diversification. Capital was also reallocated among existing Stock Pickers (away from Veritas, GQG and Metropolis, toward Jennison, Sands, Lyrical and Vulcan) in early 2026.

evidence.title: Stock Picker roster changes: ARGA and SGA replaced
evidence.summary: WTW removed ARGA and SGA as Stock Pickers due to operational issues and personnel changes respectively, replacing them with Brown Advisory and Artisan Partners to improve portfolio quality and diversification. Capital was also reallocated among existing Stock Pickers (away from Veritas, GQG and Metropolis, toward Jennison, Sands, Lyrical and Vulcan) in early 2026.
evidence.quote: ARGA had some operational issues, and SGA has been going through some personnel changes, which reduced our conviction in the two Stock Pickers.

initiatives.name: UK Government Retail Investor Engagement Campaign
initiatives.summary: The Company is participating in the UK government's marketing campaign aimed at encouraging more people to move from cash savings into investing, alongside adding new educational website content for novice investors. This is a stakeholder engagement/marketing initiative rather than a core strategic transformation.

evidence.title: Government investing campaign participation to boost retail investor engagement
evidence.summary: The Company is participating in the UK government's marketing campaign aimed at encouraging more people to move from cash savings into investing, alongside adding new educational website content for novice investors. This is a stakeholder engagement/marketing initiative rather than a core strategic transformation.
evidence.quote: To the same end, we will also be participating in the government's marketing campaign to persuade more people in the UK to move beyond cash savings into investing.

initiatives.name: Tokenisation of Assets Monitoring
initiatives.summary: The Nomination Committee identified tokenisation of assets as a topic for ongoing monitoring and future director training, reflecting awareness of emerging digital finance trends, though no concrete implementation has begun.

evidence.title: Monitoring tokenisation of assets as emerging trend
evidence.summary: The Nomination Committee identified tokenisation of assets as a topic for ongoing monitoring and future director training, reflecting awareness of emerging digital finance trends, though no concrete implementation has begun.
evidence.quote: The Committee identified a number of topics for future training sessions including training on the new internal control declaration required under the AIC Code and ongoing monitoring of industry developments relating to the tokenisation of assets.
